notes:
Batch F (trimethoprim, co-trimoxazole, dapsone, hydroxychloroquine, methotrexate). All quotes checked FOUND against fetched text using lib/text.mjs (same as fetchtext --check). ACCESS: emc search pages intermittently returned an 'are you human?' captcha page with HTTP 200; product SmPC pages were fine. emc lists no single-agent trimethoprim TABLET SmPC, so the tablet SmPC is the Teva PDF from the MHRA Products site (blob URL that products.mhra.gov.uk links to). SOURCE TYPE: 'rcophth' (Royal College of Ophthalmologists guideline PDF, December 2020, review date December 2023) is not in the schema type list; the brief allowed it as a UK authoritative source. CONFLICTS: (1) Trimethoprim breastfeeding: Teva tablet SmPC 'not contra-indicated for short term use' vs Pinewood suspension SmPC 'contraindicated if the breast fed infant is less than 4 months'. (2) Trimethoprim lower age: tablet SmPC 'children under 4 months' vs suspension SmPC 'neonates under 6 weeks'. (3) Trimethoprim porphyria: tablet 'caution' vs suspension 'should be avoided'. (4) Trimethoprim + methotrexate: tablet SmPC 'use should be avoided' vs suspension SmPC only 'increase the risk of haematologic toxicity' (SPS: avoid). (5) Teva tablet SmPC is internally inconsistent: tablet 'not suitable' under 6 years (acute section) and under 12 years (prophylaxis section). Its renal table is garbled by PDF layout, so renal thresholds are quoted from the suspension SmPC; both label the column 'eGFR (ml/min)' (not mL/min/1.73 m2). (6) Co-trimoxazole SmPC says avoid in infants younger than 8 weeks (breastfeeding section) while 4.3 and the paediatric suspension allow use from 6 weeks. Co-trimoxazole + methotrexate: co-trimoxazole SmPC only says a folate supplement should be considered; SPS says avoid; Mercury methotrexate SmPC says should not be used concomitantly. (7) Hydroxychloroquine: SmPC requires baseline eye exam and at least 12-monthly exams, max 6.5 mg/kg/day by IDEAL body weight; RCOphth (2020) and SPS say baseline eye testing is no longer recommended, annual monitoring after 5 years (after 1 year with risk factors), dose ideally under 5 mg/kg/day; SPS says by ACTUAL body weight. Pregnancy: SmPC 'should be avoided ... except when' vs BUMPS 'can be used in pregnancy if recommended by a specialist'. (8) Methotrexate: RA maximum weekly dose 25 mg (Orion tablet, Metoject) vs 20 mg (Mercury tablet). Contraception: Orion/Metoject women 6 months, men 3 months; Mercury 4.3 says 6 months for men AND women (its own 4.6 says 3 months for men); BUMPS says wait at least 3 months before trying to conceive. Mercury renal contraindication is dose-banded (CrCl under 30 for doses under 100 mg/m2; under 60 for doses over 100 mg/m2). SPS monitoring pages (methotrexate, hydroxychloroquine) state they are being updated to the November 2025 BSR guideline. NOT FOUND / NOT VERIFIED: an MHRA 2023 Drug Safety Update on methotrexate contraception (not found by DSU keyword search or the gov.uk search API); no MHRA DSU for trimethoprim, co-trimoxazole or dapsone; no SPS breastfeeding page for any batch-F medicine (SPS breastfeeding list checked); no SPS monitoring page for dapsone; no BUMPS leaflets for co-trimoxazole or dapsone (404). The dapsone SmPC gives no blood-count interval (only 'regular blood counts') and no renal guidance. UKTIS monographs and NICE were not used. BRAND PRESCRIBING: none stated by any source for these medicines. GROUP MEMBERSHIP for medicines outside batch F (clarithromycin, amoxicillin, omeprazole, atorvastatin, simvastatin, ibuprofen, naproxen, spironolactone, warfarin) is quoted from the batch-F SmPCs/SPS pages listed. Rules that reference group:ace-inhibitor, group:potassium-supplement, group:diuretic, group:oral-antidiabetic and group:antacid rely on other batches for membership. AUDIT 2026-10-17 (second checker, see audit/F.md): rules for 4.3 items worded "should not be given/administered" were raised to contraindicated (co-trimoxazole severe liver impairment, acute porphyria, drug-induced immune thrombocytopenia, first 6 weeks of life; trimethoprim infant age limits). Trimethoprim renal measure kept as eGFR (both SmPCs name eGFR; unit printed as ml/min); eGFR 15-30 band now includes 30. Trimethoprim breastfeeding and porphyria rules are no longer formulation-scoped (both SmPC statements concern the drug, and the engine defaults to the first formulation). Methotrexate: Mercury tablet SmPC 4.3 contraindications added (liver disease incl. fibrosis/cirrhosis/hepatitis; antifolate drugs, tablets; 6-month contraception); ciprofloxacin interaction raised to avoid (ciprofloxacin SmPC emc-4346, batch E); separate avoid rule for PPIs with HIGH-dose methotrexate. Cross-batch source cited: emc-4346 (batch E). ENGINE NOTE: allergen group expansion adds all ingredients of member medicines, so a recorded group:sulfonamide or co-trimoxazole allergy also produces the token trimethoprim and flags trimethoprim (own-allergy rule, contraindicated) although SPS says trimethoprim is not a sulfonamide.
CROSS-BATCH GROUP AUDIT 2026-10-17 (audit/groups-cross-batch.md): hydroxychloroquine is now a member of group hepatotoxic (its own SmPC 4.4: serious drug-induced liver injury including fulminant hepatic failure with fatal cases). The methotrexate hepatotoxic 'avoid' rule now has otherExcept hydroxychloroquine: the Metoject PEN SmPC (emc 5443) says an increase in methotrexate toxicity is in general not expected when it is given with other antirheumatic medicines, naming hydroxychloroquine (new info rule methotrexate:interaction:hydroxychloroquine). Naproxen and celecoxib (also new hepatotoxic members) are excepted too because the methotrexate NSAID rule (SPS: caution on specialist advice) covers them, as for the nephrotoxic rule.
